heroHeadline: Day 644: US DOJ Indicts Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya + 9 Officials for Chapitos Conspiracy — First Sitting Mexican Governor Charged in US History
heroSubtitle: 644 days of cartel civil war — April 30: The US Department of Justice (SDNY) unsealed a 34-page federal indictment charging Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other current or former Mexican officials with drug trafficking conspiracy and weapons charges on behalf of Los Chapitos — the first time a sitting Mexican state governor has been federally indicted in US history. Co-defendants include the Mayor of Culiacán (Juan de Dios Gámez Mendívil, alleged to have ordered police to escort Chapitos drug shipments), the former Security Secretary (Gerardo Mérida Sánchez, alleged to have warned the cartel of 10 imminent drug-lab raids in exchange for $100k/month USD), and seven additional officials. The indictment is the culmination of a sustained week of maximum US pressure: April 20 visa restrictions on 75 cartel associates, April 24 OFAC precursor-network sanctions, April 28 Los Mochis visit previewing indictments, April 29 CJNG 'El Jardinero' capture. El Mayo EDNY sentencing: May 18. Running conflict toll: ~2,425+ since Sep 9, 2024.
